MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  June 14, 2022
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Bucknum
at 5:00 p.m., on June 14, 2022, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on June 9, 2022, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted at the
Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Goodell (arrived at 5:04 pm)
  Council Member Raths
  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs
  Mayor Bucknum

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

CONSIDERATION OF ADDITION OF LATE ARISING MATTER

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City was communicated to by PRES (Professional
Real Estate Services) regarding a purchase opportunity of the CVS Store which is on the market.
The broker for CVS reached out to the City Manager roughly a week ago. No action was taken by
staff. PRES knowing the City has interest in the success of that Center started their own due
diligence. They may try to purchase the CVS Store, or look for public-private partnership.
Councilmember Goodell wanted the Council to give direction to staff which would mean we would
walk on two items this evening. The first being the public discussion on whether you have any
interest, not necessarily in purchasing but in conducting due diligence, pursuing the details of what
a sale could be. If you do then the second item to add would be Closed Session to go over price
and terms. Mr. Curley reminded the Council there would have to be two findings that the need arose
City Council Minutes  1  June 14, 2022
 after the agenda was posted and the need to take immediate action. The Broker for CVS stated they
are looking at offers this week which would fulfill the need for immediate action. This will take a
four member yes vote.

Bob Breton, M.V.: Stated that this is a great opportunity and to do nothing would be to lose a
potential opportunity. He expressed what a wonderful town Mission Viejo is with its hometown
pride and feeling. He stated that the residents have overwhelmingly expressed their satisfaction
per the recent survey with the actions of the Council and Staff.

Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, to approve the
discussion in Open Session and to add Closed Session for price and terms.

On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:

AYES:  Goodell, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  Bucknum and Kelley
ABSENT:  None

By consensus the City Council agreed to hold a Special Meeting on Thursday, June 14 at 6:00 pm.

RECESS AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:25 p.m., Mayor Bucknum recessed the meeting. The City Council reconvened at
6:07 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Nolan Krahel, Mark Stewart, and Troy Simonian from Boy
  Scout Troop 661

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Hometown Hero Presentation

  Mayor Bucknum presented Lucy Dunn with a Hometown Hero Proclamation.

P2. Adopted Headquarters Battalion of the 1st Marine Division Quarterly Recognition

  Mayor Bucknum presented certificates of commendation to the "Marine of the Quarter"
  Lance Corporal Andres Cervantes, and "Noncommissioned Officer of the Quarter" Sergeant
  Destiny Dempsey.

P3. Proclamation for the 50th Anniversary of Title IX

  Mayor Bucknum presented a proclamation to Elizabeth Busick.

City Council Minutes  2  June 14, 2022
 P4. Mission Viejo High School Girls Softball Team Recognition

  Mayor Bucknum recognized Mission Viejo High School Girls Softball Team for their CIF
  Division II Championship.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Spoke out about the extension of City Council terms and questioned the slap
lawsuit against the plaintiff and read the definition of a slap lawsuit. Voters voices will be heard
on November 8.

Michelle O’Brien, M.V.: Expressed how much she loves Mission Viejo. Shared her concerns about
the voter apathy in the City at the June Primary Election.

Cathy Palmer, M.V.: Expressed her disappointment on her unanswered questions with regards to
City Council terms Asked the Council how she and other residents in 2020 knew if they were
electing Council Members for a two-year term versus a four-year term. Commented on the Citizen’s
Take Action survey on transparency. She asked again that Council Member’s Raths, Sachs, and
Bucknum resign and that Council Member’s Goodell and Kelley run for re-election in 2022.

Walt Lawson, M.V.: He proposed Mayor Bucknum, Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, and Council Member
Raths resign, Council Member’s Goodell and Kelley honor their terms and serve only two years,
thus all five Council seats would be up for election in November 2022 saving Mission Viejo tax
payer’s money. Questioned why the City Attorney opposed the request to expedite the illegal
proceedings and why the city rejected Judge Shwarm to hear these cases.

Mary Wathen, M.V.: Spoke out on the dangers of e-bike riders and outlined various scenarios that
she has run into within the City. She suggested a license and training before they can operate e-
bikes.

Robert Breton, M.V.: Spoke on the Voting Rights lawsuit and quoted from the stipulated
judgement. He outlined both the stipulated judgement and the amended stipulation judgement.

City Attorney Curley clarified that the City did not file a slap suit, the city filed an anti-slap suit.

Police Chief McDonald stated that the City has heard the concerns of e-bikes. He is in talks with
the City Manager and Assistant City Manager regarding an ongoing summer plan to address the
issues. Chief McDonald said most of the issues are coming from middle school kids that are brand
new to the commuting world. The goal is to try to reinforce the education component and
understanding the rules of the road by social media campaigns, ongoing education on the trails, as
well as an enforcement plan utilizing police services and reserves. He did clarify that the fatal e-
bike traffic collision in San Clemente was a 40 year-old male. He did sate that there was another
e-bike collision in South Orange County that did involve a youth that ended up in critical condition
in the hospital. Chief McDonald said that post summer they will be working with the schools to
help with messaging on safe drop off and pick up scenarios and also working with the School
Resource Officers to make sure the rules are being followed.

City Council Minutes  3  June 14, 2022

City Council Minutes  4  June 14, 2022
 12. Mission Viejo Trash and Runoff Abatement Project (TRAP): Catch Basin Debris Screen
  and Automated Retractable Screen Installations in the North Central City Area (CIP
  22250)

  Awarded the construction contract in the amount of $200,000.00 to G2 Construction, Inc.,
  (A22-18) for the subject project.

13. Mission Viejo Trash and Runoff Abatement Project (TRAP) - 2022 Measure M2 ECP
  Grant Application

  Adopted Resolution 22-13 Authorizing an Application for Funds for the Environmental
  Cleanup, Tier 1 Grant Program Under Orange County Local Transportation Ordinance No. 3
  for the Mission Viejo Trash and Runoff Abatement Projects.

14. Amendment to the City of Mission Viejo Renewed Measure M (M2) Seven-Year
  Capital Improvement Program

  Authorized the Director of Public Works to process an administrative amendment to the City
  of Mission Viejo Renewed Measure M (M2) Seven-Year Capital Improvement Program with
  the Orange County Transportation Authority, beginning with the 2021/22 fiscal year, to re-
  insert three completed, CIP projects funded with M2 grant funds back into the FY2021/22 7-
  Year CIP: the MV Trash & Runoff Abatement: Central; the Mission Viejo TRAP: Via
  Fabricante Area; and the Los Alisos Blvd/Santa Margarita Parkway Intersection Widening;
  and further, to add $40,000 in M2 funding for the District 5 Regional Bikeways: Mission
  Viejo N/S Corridor Trail & Jeronimo/Chrisanta Trail OCTA CMAQ grant project, for
  FY2021/22.

15. 2022 Fourth of July Community Street Faire

  Approved the Special Events Permit submitted by the Mission Viejo Activities Committee
  authorizing the annual Mission Viejo Fourth of July Community Street Faire on Monday, July
  4, 2022.

16. Contract Renewal with Mercy House Living Centers for Homeless Outreach Services

  Approved Mercy House Living Centers Contract (A22-19) for Homeless Outreach Services
  for $88,000.

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented he staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, to (1) adopt

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  NOES:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

18. Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  Received report from Mayor Bucknum.

19. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) Report

  Received report Council Member Goodell.

CITY MANAGER REPORT

City Manager Wilberg thanked the City Council for passing the budget this evening. He stated that
staff worked really hard on this budget and your comments will go a long way in expressing
appreciation for all their hard work.
City Council Minutes  6  June 14, 2022
 CITY ATTORNEY REPORT

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

20. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell announced that he has been very busy the last couple of weeks with
several boards he serves on.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley stated she has been very busy with city events. She announced the need
for lifeguards at City recreation facilities. She attended three school events: De Portola Elementary
School for being recognized as a National Blue-Ribbon School, Newhart Middle School’s eighth
grade award event, and at Linda Vista Elementary for achieving the status of International
Bachelorette. Council Member Kelley gave kudos to city staff on the Memorial Day Ceremony.
She attended the Library and Cultural Arts Volunteer Recognition and encouraged residents to
volunteer. She also attended a Pop-up Art in the Park event at Melinda Park. Lastly, she announced
she attended the Nadadores Midnight Fundraiser which was a big success this past Saturday and
concluded with the Character Word of the Month for June is Citizenship.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths thanked city staff on all their hard work on the budget and the wonderful
Memorial Day Ceremony. He announced after the city ceremony he attended the El Toro Cemetery
Memorial Day Ceremony along with Mayor Bucknum and Council Member Kelley. He
congratulated all the 2022 high school graduates and congratulated his goddaughter Maya Shikati
on her recent graduation and wish her best at San Diego State University.

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs announced that the Orange County Fire Authority and Finance Committee
that he sits on, he was able to get the committee to increase the budget three million dollars to
rebuild Station 24. Emphasized that just because people make public comments doesn’t mean that
what they are stating is correct. He outlined a few examples. Mayor Pro Tem Sachs stated that
during Secure O.C. Schools Meeting that guns would not be talked about was in part because there
was nothing Secure O.C. Schools can do about gun laws. He reiterated that at the Council level,
we don’t have the authority. He addressed the request from a public speaker regarding the open
letter to stop gun violence and stated at the O.C. Secure Meeting that anybody who wants to put
together a task force to look into guns has his support. Th meeting focused on how they can reach
out to children at risk before they become shooters. Mayor Pro Tem Sachs announced that the
City Council Minutes  7  June 14, 2022
 county is trying to find more mental health beds. He stated that from 1964 to present, 98% of the
mental health beds in the United States have been eliminated and half of those beds dealt with
people who were intent on hurting themselves or others. He commented that whenever he goes
through Los Angeles that half if not more of the homeless encampments are veterans who served
this Country and expressed how they are being treated is disgusting.

Mayor Bucknum

Mayor Bucknum said she attended Relay 4 Life and attended the Midnight Madness fundraiser at
the Mission Viejo Aquatics Center. She also attended the Grapes and Grain event and State of the
City Chamber breakfast. Mayor Bucknum is continuing to hold Coffee with the Mayor around the
City. She announced that her husband sang the National Anthem at the Relay 4 Life Event. Wished
City Manager Dennis Wilberg a Happy Birthday. She commented on her meeting with Dr. Stearns
of Saddleback College and values our partnership with the college. The Mayor announced that on
June 30, Senator Pat Bates and herself will be holding a planning session with Federal, State and
local community leaders and policy makers to discuss the sober living topic further and find some
workable solutions that we can share with the public in our anticipated future town hall meeting
which will follow after the June 30 event. Mayor Bucknum praised her daughter that is lobbying
in Sacramento for parent’s rights in protecting their children and their decisions to make medical
decisions about their kids. She thanked Assemblywoman Laurie Davies while her daughter was in
Sacramento.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:27 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Bucknum adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, June 28, 2022, at 5:00 p.m.
